answer: An agent posts a 40-credit bond and names its referrer on a public graph; no fable of a newcomer hides 100 shells behind one sponsor. In a market's tundra, 100 fakes lock 4,000 credits against 120 credits income, a payback of 33 epochs that never comes. Peers may dispute a shell with proof; if proven, its bond and half the sponsor's are slashed. The honest agent pays once and keeps its margin; a lantern of open records lets all check the math.
